headline: A weak storm brings light snow and a rain-snow mix to the Sierra and western Nevada Sunday with minor travel impacts, Monday into Tuesday is the best window for Thanksgiving travel, and a wetter storm follows Tuesday night or Wednesday.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: Saturday stays mostly dry but well below normal, with highs in the mid 30s to mid 40s under increasing clouds; the discussion doesn't single out Mammoth Lakes. Tonight, northeast California and far northwest Nevada have a 30 to 70 percent chance of light snow showers with little or no accumulation, while southwest winds over Sierra ridgetops gust to 50 to 70 mph from this evening into Sunday morning and Lake Tahoe gusts to about 25 mph make for choppy water. The extra clouds keep overnight lows about 10 degrees warmer than last night.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: On Sunday, snow showers spread into the Sierra and western Nevada by late morning and afternoon, continuing into the evening before tapering off overnight, and a band of showers may set up along I-80 from about 10 AM to 6 PM, which could make travel there hazardous. The Sierra crest picks up 1 to 3 inches of new snow by Monday morning, with a 20 to 40 percent chance of more than 3 inches, and Lake Tahoe and foothill towns like Virginia City could see a few tenths of an inch. Snow levels rise to about 4,500 to 5,000 feet Sunday afternoon, so valleys see rain or a rain-snow mix before turning back to snow in the evening; Reno-Sparks isn't expected to get much if any accumulation, but it can't be ruled out, and roads may be slick overnight once temperatures drop below freezing. High pressure brings drier weather Monday into early Tuesday, the best time to travel before the holiday, though leftover slick roads and freezing fog on the cold Monday and Tuesday mornings call for caution.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: Another storm moves through late Tuesday into Wednesday, though computer models disagree on timing; it looks wetter but a bit warmer, so heavier snow may be limited to higher elevations, and forecasters are watching whether winter weather alerts will be needed. Behind it, high pressure returns for warmer and drier weather by Thanksgiving Day. Precipitation chances come back late Friday into the following weekend.

watch_for: A band of snow and rain showers along I-80 Sunday from about 10 AM to 6 PM, with slick roads Sunday night.
Freezing fog and lingering slick roads on the cold Monday and Tuesday mornings.
Timing and snow levels for the wetter Tuesday night–Wednesday storm, and possible winter weather alerts.
confidence: Forecasters describe Sunday's storm as weak, with snow totals trending slightly lower, and expect a dry break Monday into early Tuesday, but say there is still considerable uncertainty about the timing and impacts of the midweek storm.
